messages.subject: Problem with the creation of a camera station table
messages.subject_clean: Problem with the creation of a camera station table
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

Like several others, I imported my data from an existing Excel file. While my species table is working perfectly fine with camtrapR, I'm encountering a problem with the camera station table. I can't perform any functions with it because it doesn't register as a dataframe and I keep getting the following warning message:

> Error: CTtable must be a data.frame
> In addition: Warning message:
> In if (class(CTtable) != "data.frame") stop("CTtable must be a data.frame",  :
>   the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used

Attached is the table I've constructed in Excel that mimics the camtraps table and has the necessary columns for species, station, co-ordinates, setup and retrieval dates.

Is there something I can do in order to get this to work?

Thanks so much for your help!
Ayesha

I'm trying to create a record table initially, based on how I have arranged my "directory". This was images saved in to a main folder and two sub folders as: camera station - species - number of individuals. I think creating a record table hasn't worked how I want due to the additional subfolder of number of individuals of that species,  seen at each station.

Many thanks in advance
H

messages.subject: tidyverse and camtrapR compatibility
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,
in a recent thread <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/camtrapr/YEB5lX4IeCw>, Ayesha and David started a discussion about the compatibility of camtrapR with the tidyverse world. Is that be relevant for many users? And what exactly would you wish for in terms of compatibility?

Here's an idea for how to make camtrapR compatible with tidyverse. It would require a lot of rewriting to make the functions of camtrapR utilize tibbles directly, so I believe the simplest option for now would be to detect if the user provides a tibble as input and if so, automatically convert it to a data frame internally for processing them in camtrapR. Then, if the input was a tibble, the output data frame can also be converted to a tibble automatically.
Would it be sufficient for your compatibility needs?

My feeling so far is that it would be helpful and I can try to look into it when I have some time. But I'd love to hear your thoughts about this issue first.

Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: tidyverse and camtrapR compatibility
messages.body_plain:
Jürgen
I recall I had a lot of grief because when I first brought the excel version of my recordTable into camtrapR as a "tible", not realising that this was not a simple base R data frame.  Ayesha had the same experience.

So my request is - can camtrapR detect when it is being given a "tible" and give a more explicate and earlier warning that camtrapR use base R data frames?
and/or,
can the (excellent) vignette explain that if you are importing a recordTable you must use the class data frame only; read.csv NOT read_xl or read_csv

I am emphatically not suggesting camtrapR be modified to use 'tible' and tidy verse. One of the strengths of camtrapR is that the vignette is so good that an R-beginner can use camtrapR and R.  But a lot of the R learning materials lead one to tidyverse  and that is not helpful with camtrapR.

David

Hi,

messages.subject: Re: Folder organisation - subfolders
messages.body_plain:
Hi Helen & Lucia,
when you use the species folder approach for identifying species, you cannot have subfolders within the species folders. This is because camtrapR will use the folder name as the species name. So I suppose the entries in the species column are "1", "2", etc.?

Lucia is right, it would be easier to add group size and other information with the metadata tagging approach. Even though you identified images by folder already, you can still add other metadata tags for additional information (like group size) to the images, it will be reported in the record table.

Here is a possible way forward in your situation:

1. assign the group size to all images as metadata. I'm afraid you'll have to do this manually in digiKam, but you can assign the group size to all images in a group size subfolder at once. It may be possible to write some exiftool code to do this, but I don't have any code ready to achieve this)
2. move all images from the group size subfolders to the species folders. That can be automated in R. Below is some code for that purpose (please test if first or make a backup before applying the code):

Let us know how it goes please
Cheers,
Jürgen

library(stringi)

# define image directory
wd_images_ID <- "..."   # define image directory

# find all image filenames
filenames_full <- list.files(wd_images_ID, full.names = TRUE, recursive = TRUE, pattern = ".JPG$")
filenames_short <- basename(filenames_full)

# find their directories
directory_of_files <- dirname(filenames)

# make data.frame
df_tmp <- data.frame(filename_full = filenames_full,
                     directory = directory_of_files,
                     filename_short = filenames_short,
                     directory_to = NA,
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# find last character of directory name
last_character <- stri_sub(df_tmp$directory, from = -1, to = -1)

# which images are in a group size directory (drectory name end with a number)?   # gives a warning but that's ok
which_last_character_number <- which(!is.na <http://is.na>(as.numeric(last_character)))

# define output directory: if image is in a group size directory, find its parent diretory (species directory), Otherwise change nothing
df_tmp$directory_to[which_last_character_number]  <- dirname(df_tmp$directory[which_last_character_number])
df_tmp$directory_to[-which_last_character_number] <- df_tmp$directory[-which_last_character_number]

# move files from group size to species directory (does not rename in this case, only moves files)
file.rename(from = df_tmp$filename_full[which_last_character_number],
            to = file.path(df_tmp$directory_to, df_tmp$filename_short)[which_last_character_number])
